concept.title: Adaptive and mobility equipment
concept.shortdesc: Getting, trying, hiring or adapting equipment, aids and clothing that help disabled people with mobility, sensory needs and daily living.

conbody.note: Draft category. The name and definition were written by a language model from a clustering of real service descriptions, and no person has reviewed them.

ul.li: daily living aids and assistive technology
help choosing a wheelchair or riser chair
advice and information on disability and mobility: belongs in a neighbouring group that is not yet a category (information only, not equipment itself)
buying or repairing mobility equipment: belongs in a neighbouring group that is not yet a category (retail and servicing of mobility products)
reablement and rehabilitation care: belongs in a neighbouring group that is not yet a category (care and therapy rather than equipment)

section.title: Evidence and status

strow.stentry: Draft, not reviewed, and unconfirmed: the group did not re-form reliably (stability 0.47). It is named only because a need points at it.
Lancashire (19), Bristol (5), North Lincolnshire (2), Shropshire (2), Dorset (1)
Provider-concentrated: one organisation holds 56%. It may be one organisation's wording rather than a real category.
Did not recur reliably when the data was resampled; it is named only because a need points at it, so treat the name as a proposal and the group as unconfirmed.

section.p: Identifier in this run: svc-048. Identifiers are cluster numbers of one run and change whenever the clustering is re-run; they are not stable ids.
